sections.text: The US government has suspended Microsoft and seven other technology firms, including Adobe, from a program that helps foreign workers obtain permanent US residency. Vice President JD Vance accused the companies of abusing the H-1B visa system to replace American workers with cheaper foreign labour. The Department of Labor announced it will not process new or pending applications from these firms.

sections.text: Vance claimed Microsoft laid off American workers while filing thousands of visa applications, undercutting domestic wages. Microsoft rejected these allegations, stating that eighty per cent of its H-1B filings were for existing employees rather than new hires, and that its international staff receive the same compensation as US workers. Immigration advocacy groups argue that attracting global talent benefits the US economy, while Vance described the visa recipients as "indentured servants".

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Eighty-seven-year-old Maricarmen Abascal died in hospital two weeks after being removed on a stretcher from her Madrid home of over seven decades. The flat's owner had significantly raised her rent, which exceeded her pension. Although the firm later offered a return agreement, Abascal died before signing. sections.text: Abascal became a national symbol of the housing crisis. Tens of thousands protested, setting up encampments in Madrid and other cities. gist: Presenter Alison Hammond feared she was having a heart attack during a live broadcast.

Hammond returned to the show a week later to discuss her experience.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: During a live broadcast of ITV's This Morning last Friday, presenter Alison Hammond rushed off air after experiencing what she feared was a heart attack. She was taken to hospital, where tests revealed she had actually suffered a panic attack. Hammond described the experience as "very real" and one of the scariest things she had ever been through.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident highlighted the intense pressure of presenting live television. Returning to the show a week later, Hammond and psychologist Dr Sian Williams discussed panic attacks to raise awareness. Williams explained that panic attacks represent "anxiety on overdrive" and can feel identical to heart attacks due to shared physical symptoms like chest pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Hammond has returned to her regular presenting slot on This Morning. She noted that the health scare has given her a new perspective, prompting her to take stock of her health.

Signal boss Whittaker vows to leave markets if forced to weaken encryption.
Whittaker advocates for robust privacy protections despite misuse challenges.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Meredith Whittaker criticised AI doom narratives, pointing instead to the real dangers of careless technology use, such as faulty intelligence nearly causing a war. She also defended end-to-end encryption against government demands for backdoors and discussed past activism against military AI contracts.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Careless AI implementation risks flawed targeting and military escalation. Meanwhile, weakening encryption threatens user privacy globally, exposing vulnerable people to state surveillance and authoritarian overreach, though privacy tools can occasionally be exploited by bad actors.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Signal stated it would leave any country that forces it to compromise user encryption. The UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology is preparing legislation regarding messaging apps and safety.
